editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a fancy university where a mean professor wants to tear down your dorm just to build a hotel. That is exactly what happens to Mitsugu Kimura and his roommates at Sigma House. You get a great mix of characters here, from the straight-A student to the absolute slackers who can barely pass a quiz. The vibe is super energetic and feels like a classic underdog story. It is all about a group of misfits who have to put their heads together to pull off the most insane cheating scheme you have ever seen just to save their home.

What really makes this movie pop is the fast pacing and the funny ways they try to trick the system. Seeing J-pop icon Namie Amuro on screen is a cool treat, and her energy fits the movie perfectly. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated since it is from the 90s, the heart of the story still works. If you love movies about students fighting the system, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the end, the students use every trick in the book to cheat on their exams. They manage to outsmart Professor Migita by using their teamwork and some wild physical stunts. They all get the grades they need, which stops the professor from tearing down Sigma House. The corrupt professor gets exposed for his hotel plot, and the students celebrate their victory. It ends on a high note with the dorm saved and the slackers finally winning.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and school comedies.
